To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the spectrum of a covariance matrix determines the generalization risk in ridge and ridgeless regression, and the multiple descents in the risk curve can be eliminated by the optimal ridge regularization.

(1) the generalization risk in linear regression can increase and then decreases with more data samples; (2) this phenomenon is caused by the spectrum of the data covariance matrix; (3) this phenomenon occurs when the spectrum is highly ill-condition.
the spectrum of a covariance matrix determines the bias and variance of ridge regression and ridgeless linear regressions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following two problems:
the generalization risk and sample-wise multiple descent in the linear regression problem.

the following three questions: (a) what is the bias-variance tradeoff in the high-dimensional regime? (b) does the generalization risk exhibit the multiple descent phenomenon in the high-dimensional setting, and (c) can we eliminate multiple descent with regularization?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in general, the generalization performance of ridge and ridge-less linear regression is highly sensitive to the spectrum of the data covariance matrix.
, for a linear regression model with multivariate normally distributed features, if the spectrum of the feature covariance matrix consists of eigenvalues of growing proportionally multiplicity, then:

\emph{the generalization risk curve can exhibit multiple descent when the data features follow multivariate normal distribution, the spectrum of the data covariance matrix is ill-conditioned, and the dimension and the size of the training dataset tend to infinity proportionately}.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the generalization risk in ridge and ridgeless regression can be highly non-monotone with more training data, and this is caused by the ill-conditioned spectrum of the covariance of the data features.
we characterize the limiting bias-variance of the generalization error for the linear ridge regression with multivariate normal features and highly ill-conditioned covariance matrix.

the generalization risk is a non-monotone function of the number of data samples, and the ridge estimator with an optimal regularization parameter can make the generalization risk a monotone function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spectrum of a covariance matrix is a crucial determinant of the sample-wise multiple-descent phenomenon of the generalizability of ridge and ridge-less linear regression.
spectral multiplicity entails sample-wise multiple descent of the ridge regression estimator.
the generalization risk is not always a monotonically decreasing function of the number of training data samples, and that the ridge estimator can eliminate multiple descent.
